title: One record, both renderers, in the workspace
caption: `pg-order`, generated from `sales.order` on PostgreSQL as the order form's own account and published through the administrator plane, in the host page's workspace: the forms the person may read, the form's records in an AG Grid Community grid, and the open record drawn by `@formancy/react` and `@formancy/angular` from one definition through `@formancy/data-client` ([0047](./docs/decisions/0047-a-hosts-workspace-lists-opens-and-edits-records-in-linked-grids.md)). The order's id, “9007199254740993”, is 2^53+1, which a JavaScript number reads back as …992, and its amount, “99999999999999.9999”, is the largest `numeric(18,4)` holds. Both panes show both digit for digit, because exact values travel as strings ([0008](./docs/decisions/0008-exact-values-travel-as-strings.md)).
alt: The host page's workspace: Forms naming pg-order, the Records grid with the order 9007199254740993 open, and below it the record, loaded “into both forms.”: the same order form twice, React and Angular, each showing customer “Muster AG”, id 9007199254740993 and amount 99999999999999.9999.

title: Both renderers, before any server
caption: The examples page runs the generator in the browser over a snapshot captured from PostgreSQL, with no server, and renders `sales.order` with both renderers. An amount with five decimals for a `numeric(18,4)` column is refused in both with the same sentence, “Enter it in the form this question asks for.”, and the empty required fields with “This question needs an answer.” ([0021](./docs/decisions/0021-generated-forms-preview-in-both-frameworks.md)).
alt: Two order forms on white paper, labelled React and Angular, each with Status placed, Amount 12.34567 refused as not in the form the question asks for, Customer and Order date refused as unanswered, and a count under each box with a limit.

title: Connect
caption: On SQL Server, as an account without VIEW DEFINITION. What the catalog hid from it comes first, each gap “cannot tell”, not “does not exist”, so a table or key missing below is never taken as absent ([0004](./docs/decisions/0004-a-snapshot-says-what-it-could-not-see.md), [0007](./docs/decisions/0007-sqlserver-discovery-and-what-it-hides.md)).
alt: The studio's Connect step for ms-reader: “SQL Server 16.0.4295.3”, discovered as formancy_reader, and a panel “What this connection could not see” listing gaps in what refers to a table, row security, objects, checks, defaults and foreign keys.

title: Choose
caption: As the order form's own account. A foreign key is offered as a lookup only where this account may read its target: `approved_by` and `created_by` point at `sales.employee`, whose rows “cannot be offered”, and the customer columns it may not read “cannot be shown” ([0027](./docs/decisions/0027-a-snapshot-says-what-its-account-may-do.md)).
alt: The lookups group of the Choose step: two employee keys refused because sales.employee cannot be read by this connection, and the customer lookup ticked with name as the column to show and four columns this connection may not read.

title: Generate
caption: The generator says what it chose and what it refused, kind by kind, from what this account may do: a column it may not update is “Read-only on update”, and “Row-level security applies” to it on `sales.customer`, named as the database's own limit ([0009](./docs/decisions/0009-generation-is-deterministic-and-says-what-it-chose.md), [0027](./docs/decisions/0027-a-snapshot-says-what-its-account-may-do.md)).
alt: The generator's notes: create, update and delete offered, nothing blocked, read-only notes for id, customer, order_date, amount and created_by, the inferred controls with their column types, and an access note that row-level security applies on sales.customer.

title: Policy
caption: The tenant pin becomes a row filter on the orders this form reaches and on the customers its list may offer, taken from the signed-in person's attributes “and never from the form”; a customer outside the filter is refused on save “even by somebody who knows its key” ([0011](./docs/decisions/0011-every-operation-carries-a-trusted-policy-context.md)).
alt: Two policy groups, each with tenant_id equal to the trusted attribute tenant: the row filters on sales.order and the rows the Customer list may offer, under which an unticked box offers to reach only the orders whose Customer is one of these.

title: Order lines through their order
caption: A form over `sales.order_line`, which has no tenant column, discovered as the fixture's owner because the order form's own account may not read the lines. Its Order list is filtered to the person's tenant; ticked, the box “Only rows of sales.order_line whose Order is one of these” makes another tenant's line not found on read and update, and “A row that names none is reached by nobody.” Unticked, the step notes that nothing scopes the rows; nothing requires the box ([0043](./docs/decisions/0043-a-child-forms-rows-are-reached-only-through-a-parent-its-policy-admits.md)).
alt: The group Rows the Order list may offer, on the Policy step of a form over sales.order_line: a filter of tenant_id equal to the trusted attribute tenant, and the box “Only rows of sales.order_line whose Order is one of these”, ticked, with its hint.

title: Presentation
caption: Labels, help text, order, section and width are a patch over the generated form: every row names the column it is bound to and may move to the other section, nothing here adds, removes or renames a field, and an empty label is refused: “A label needs words a person can read.” ([0030](./docs/decisions/0030-presentation-is-a-patch-over-the-generated-base.md), [0075](./docs/decisions/0075-a-field-may-move-to-another-generated-section.md)).
alt: The Presentation step's Order section below Undo, Redo and the status “Moved Customer down.”: its section label, then a row each for Order date, Customer, Status with its label emptied and refused, Amount, notes labelled Remarks at full width, Group, Created by and Approved by, each naming the column it is bound to and offering Move to Record.

title: Preview
caption: The form as the people filling it in will see it, with the labels and order chosen in Presentation, on white paper in the Blueprint theme, and checked by the released engine after Validate. The Customer list is filled only by the runtime plane, so “the renderer says where the list would be”.
alt: The Preview step: a note that the Customer list is filled by the runtime plane once published, and the order form on white paper after Validate, with notes labelled Remarks at full width, Order date and Amount marked required, and Order date, Customer and Amount each saying required.

title: A conflicting publish
caption: Another administrator, grace, published version 2 while ada worked; the capture script sends grace's request to the same server. Nothing is overwritten: “Yours was not published, and theirs is untouched.” The step says which version is published now, and “Publishing waits until you rebase on it.” ([0013](./docs/decisions/0013-published-configuration-is-files-with-link-based-swap.md)).
alt: The Publish step saying that version 2 of pg-order is published now and is somebody else's, its Publish button disabled, and an alert that somebody published version 2 while you worked, with a button “Rebase on version 2”.

title: Drift
caption: After the capture script renamed `notes` to `memo` in the captured snapshot, as discovery reports a real rename on both engines. The rename is a “possible-rename” for a person to confirm, not a guess, and restoring version 1, which still binds `notes`, is refused: “Version 1 cannot be restored: the database has changed in a way it cannot serve.” Against a database changed this way the server refuses what the report blocks ([0010](./docs/decisions/0010-drift-is-classified-against-the-bindings.md), [0030](./docs/decisions/0030-presentation-is-a-patch-over-the-generated-base.md), [0041](./docs/decisions/0041-the-runtime-refuses-what-drift-blocks.md)).
alt: The Drift step: “3 changes, 1 blocking.”; read, create and update blocked; a blocking column-dropped change for notes, review changes for the new column memo and a possible rename; version 3 offered for download; a refused restore of version 1 with what blocks it; and an import with no version file chosen yet.

title: Regenerated
caption: Regenerated from the database as it is now, keeping the presentation, and saying before anything is published what it could not carry: the label chosen for `notes`, and the policy entry that names it. “Nothing is published until you publish it.”
alt: A panel “Regenerated from version 3” listing the label Remarks dropped because notes is not in the regenerated form, and a policy entry for notes that no longer fits.

title: Carried
caption: Back in Presentation, the dropped label is offered to the new column as one edit, “which Undo takes back”; nothing carries it by guessing that `memo` is `notes`.
alt: A panel “Carried from version 3” offering to give the label Remarks to Memo (memo).

title: Restored
caption: After the capture script put the snapshot back without the rename, version 1 fits the database again and is restored as the next version, with the policy it had: “The database was not changed.”
alt: The versions panel offering version 4 for download, and saying “Restored version 1 as version 4” and that the database was not changed.

title: A key that moved
caption: The capture script renamed `order_date` to `order date` in the captured snapshot with the drift's function, which the adapters' suites compare with a real rename of `notes` only. Regenerated, the key `order_date` now names the column `order date`, and nothing can tell whether that is the same column, so its grants wait: “Keep grants for order_date”, or remove them. “Publishing waits until each is decided, and the server refuses grants nobody decided.” ([0039](./docs/decisions/0039-a-publish-says-what-happens-to-the-grants-of-reassigned-keys.md)).
alt: A notice “Keys that now stand for something else” on the Policy step: that each grant below was written for what its key stood for, that publishing waits until each is decided, the sentence “Grants for order_date were written for column order_date; it now stands for column order date.”, and buttons to keep or remove the grants for order_date.

title: The customer typeahead
caption: The customer field is the published lookup, which the generator draws as a typeahead because its label can be searched ([0066](./docs/decisions/0066-a-lookup-a-person-can-search-is-generated-as-a-typeahead.md)). As clara, a clerk of tenant 1, types, the server answers as her with the rows she may choose: “Muster AG”, and not tenant 2's Other Tenant GmbH, which matches too and has the same customer number. Each option travels under a token that is a reference, not a permission ([0012](./docs/decisions/0012-a-lookup-token-is-a-reference-not-a-permission.md)).
alt: The React pane of a new order with er typed into Customer and a list offering Muster AG alone.

title: A stale save
caption: Two drafts of one record. React saved first; Angular's save, made against the version it read, is refused as stale instead of overwriting it: “Your changes are still in the form.”, with a button to “Load the saved record” ([0015](./docs/decisions/0015-a-record-operation-is-one-guarded-statement.md)).
alt: The order form twice: the React pane says “Saved.”; the Angular pane shows a notice “Not saved”, that the record changed since it was read, that the changes are still in the form, and a button “Load the saved record”.

title: A refused choice
caption: A customer chosen from the list and deleted by somebody else before Save; the capture script inserts and deletes it through the database's owner. The server checks the choice again when the order is saved and refuses it on the field: “This is not one of the options this form offers.”
alt: The React pane of a new order with an error summary “There is 1 problem to fix” and, under Customer, the refusal.

title: A save whose answer was lost
caption: A save whose answer was lost after the server stored it: the capture script lets the server store it and then tells the page the connection was reset. The page cannot know whether it was saved, so it says so, offers to check, and holds the save; the page sends nothing again ([0031](./docs/decisions/0031-an-answer-lost-after-a-write-is-unknown.md)).
alt: The React pane with a notice “It may have been saved”, the sentence that the answer was lost between this page and the data server, and a button “Check whether it was saved”.

title: Leaving unsaved work
caption: The save whose answer was lost, above, is work a person could lose: New record would drop the form that holds it, so the workspace asks first. It names what was asked for and what each form holds, and waits: “Keep editing” changes nothing and gives the keyboard back, “Discard and continue” carries the request out. Every way of leaving a form asks the same -- another row, Load, another form, Back, Sign out, a child row and hiding a renderer ([0047](./docs/decisions/0047-a-hosts-workspace-lists-opens-and-edits-records-in-linked-grids.md)).
alt: A notice “Unsaved changes”: starting a new record closes the React form of order k1:9007199254740993, which holds “a save that may have been stored, not yet checked.”, with the buttons Keep editing and Discard and continue.

title: Deleting a record
caption: `pg-order-delete`, the getting-started job's second order form, which the capture script publishes as the job does: it grants clerks delete and names each foreign key a delete of an order acts through ([0051](./docs/decisions/0051-a-delete-reaches-other-tables-only-through-foreign-keys-the-policy-names.md)). Each row of its grid has a Delete, a real button named for its record and reached by the arrow keys. Pressed, it asks in place, under the grid, with no overlay: the question names the record, and what the delete also does is said in the server's terms -- “Other records that refer to it are deleted with it.” -- never which tables or how many. “Keep it” comes first, so the keyboard is never put on the button that deletes ([0053](./docs/decisions/0053-a-host-deletes-a-record-from-its-detail-or-its-row-after-a-confirmation-in-place.md)).
alt: A Records grid scrolled to its last column, Delete, with one order of Muster AG and its Delete button, and under the grid a confirmation “Delete Order k1:9007199254740993?” saying that it is removed from the database for everyone who can see it, that other records that refer to it are deleted with it, and the buttons Keep it and Delete it.

title: A save after the table changed
caption: After clara loaded the record, the capture script narrowed `status` from `varchar(20)` to `varchar(8)` through the database's owner, which drift review says stops create and update. Her save, which changes only the notes, is refused by the server in a sentence that names no column: “Nothing was saved; an administrator must review the form.” What she typed stays in the form, and the row is as it was ([0041](./docs/decisions/0041-the-runtime-refuses-what-drift-blocks.md)).
alt: The React pane with a notice “Not saved” saying that the database changed since this form was published, in a way this form cannot save safely, that nothing was saved and that an administrator must review the form, above the loaded order with the notes clara typed still in it.

title: Another tenant's record
caption: otto, a clerk of tenant 2, may read records with this form, and his grid says “No records.”: tenant 1's orders are not listed for him. With tenant 1's record token he is told “No such record.”, the answer a token that names no record gets, so the page learns nothing about another tenant's orders ([0022](./docs/decisions/0022-the-runtime-plane-asks-the-policy-every-time.md)).
alt: otto's Records grid saying “No records.”, and below it no record open, the record token k1:9007199254740993 under Open by record token and an alert “No such record.”.
